summary: NDR feed s176_triple is degraded: 100% VLAN tags missing (VLAN 10,20 not seen), 40.3% one-way TCP sessions, and 2.7% packet loss - NDR lacks bidirectional, segmented context for detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or SPAN/TAP source is stripping 802.1Q tags (VLAN pruning, access-port mirroring, or 'strip VLAN' policy enabled). All packets arrive untagged so required VLANs 10 and 20 are never observed.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot segment traffic by VLAN/tenant, loses context for VLAN 10,20, and misses VLAN-dependent detection logic and filtering - effectively blind to those segments.

recommended_fix.why: NDR requires VLAN 10,20 for segmentation; broker must forward 802.1Q tags intact instead of stripping them.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of many TCP sessions is delivered to this NDR port. Likely asymmetric routing with unaggregated SPANs or broker hashing that splits client->server and server->client to different tool ports, or only one side of the link is tapped.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly and stateful detection. 85/211 sessions (40.3%) one-way causes broken flows, missed handshakes, failed signature matching and increased false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Ensure both directions of each flow are aggregated/hashed to the same NDR tool port so it sees complete sessions.

findings.root_cause: 2.7% of TCP packets show gaps/retransmissions indicating drops before the NDR - typical of SPAN oversubscription/buffer exhaustion under burst or packet broker ingress drops, not tool overload (tool_overload healthy).
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR sees incomplete TCP streams, cannot reliably reassemble full payload (needs_full_payload=true), misses detections, creates incomplete flow records and noisy retransmission artifacts.

recommended_fix.why: TAP provides lossless, full-duplex capture vs lossy SPAN; eliminates SPAN drop-induced gaps and improves NDR reassembly accuracy.
